text:
The food is good, my main complaint today is the fact that no chocolate syrup was put on my mocha frappe.

IF/when I decide to spend a ridiculous amount of money on an iced mocha beverage, in a large size as well, I would hope they could take the couple seconds to put the chocolate syrup on it that it comes with, when putting the whipped cream on. Or at the very least, an explanation as to why there is no chocolate syrup.

Previous visit(s) complaints:

The atmosphere inside is never comfortable to say the least its normally dark inside especially in the mornings. 95% of the negative opinions I have about this Mcdonalds, comes from the woman security guard that usually works in the mornings.

I've thought about working here and immediately decided it was a bad idea due to this woman.

I do not wish to talk ill of her, she does her job well, but she also takes things a step way too far. Mind you, the area this mcdonalds is in is a bit dodgy, one cross street is colfax and the other is literally littered with trash and people who have no problem walking up to your car and asking if you want to buy drugs, so I understand the level of security that might be needed to uphold standards here.

That being said, i gave it a few visits to actually make my opinion on the woman security guard to give the benefit of the doubt before posting to let the world know.

First, she is very negative from my perspective, she doesnt make any effort to be friendly, even to the customers. She way she talks to people, is demands, not polite requests.

I've seen a woman park in the curbside spot, walk inside to where i was currently at, and the security guard immediately told her she cannot park there, and the woman let her know that her order was originally curbside but it wasnt working on the app so she came inside. And she scolded her, and said that she needed to move immediately because it was impeding their work area. Even though there were other curbside spots open and she was still trying to place an order and be a paying customer. The customer even responded by asking why she was so angry with her for parking there for a few minutes.

A simple solution would have been to politely ask her to move the car as soon as possible. Not to scold the customer or demand her to do things.

Another instance, a man was parked next to me, it seemed to me he was scrolling on the app getting his order together, when the security guard walked up to his car and told him to leave immediately because he had not walked inside yet. She didn't even ask him why he was there or anything. The man left and she followed his car and made sure he left.

Shes also stared out the windows to the parking lot to the point ive felt very uncomfortable before.

These are just a few things. By all means, she does a good job at her job, but needs to treat customers with more respect.

I hope if she sees what i have to say she can take it as constructive criticism. Because if she could learn to have more respect towards people i would come inside more often, and feel comfortable enough to even apply for a job at this location. Even my roommates and neighbors all agree about the atmosphere because of this woman.

Thanks for reading.
author: Brittany Montoya

text: I woke up in an alleyway after being drugged and assaulted this weekend. This McDonald’s was the first open place I could find after walking down colfax barefoot in the freezing cold. All of my possessions were gone, my clothes were ripped and I was covered in scratches and bruises. I asked if they had a phone I could use, the worker looked me up and down and gave me a dirty look then laughed and said no. A security guard approached me and stupid me felt relieved because I mistakenly believed his job was to keep people safe. He told me to leave, I asked him if he could at least please call the police for me and I would go wait down the block or something, or if he could direct me where I to go to use a phone or get any sort of help. I was terrified, in a lot of pain, freezing, and completely traumatized. He did not care in the slightest and his only concern was physically forcing a vulnerable girl back out onto colfax before the sun had even risen. I wouldn’t have even been able to keep warm on a summer night, let alone in that weather. He had a heavy jacket on and zipped up while sitting inside. Can someone tell me what exactly his job is then?? What is it that this “man” (I hesitate to even use that word, because he is incredibly far from it) is getting paid to do? I was not causing a scene or anything like that. I quietly begged him to contact the police. Trust me, last thing I wanted was any attention drawn to me. Maybe I’m being naive, but I don’t see any reason why these employees treated me so poorly or refused to do even the bare minimum by calling the cops and having me wait for them down the block…I have no faith in humanity anymore.
author: Lexi
